tex_content.html:
Lemma
1. ch4:4.4,ch4:4.11,ch4:4.12,ch4:4.13\group ch04-poisson-newtonian-potential Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0069, gilbarg-trudinger:page-0070, gilbarg-trudinger:page-0071 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0070 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0071 Let $B_1=B_R(x_0)$ and $B_2=B_{2R}(x_0)$. If $f\in C^\alpha (\overline B_2)$ and $w$ is its Newtonian potential over $B_2$, then $w\in C^{2,\alpha }(\overline B_1)$ and \begin{equation} \tag {4.11} |D^2w|'_{0,\alpha ;B_1}\leq C|f|'_{0,\alpha ;B_2}, \qquad C=C(n,\alpha ). \end{equation}
Proof

\sketch Formula (4.9) and the kernel estimates first give

\begin{equation} \tag {4.12} |D^2w(x)|\leq C\bigl(|f(x)|+R^\alpha [f]_{\alpha ;B_2}\bigr). \end{equation}

For $x,\bar x\in B_1$, split the difference of the two formulas into the ball of radius $|x-\bar x|$ about their midpoint and its complement. Hölder control handles the near integrals; the mean-value estimate for $D^2\Gamma $ and integration by parts handle the far and boundary terms. Thus

\begin{equation} \tag {4.13} |D^2w(x)-D^2w(\bar x)| \leq C\bigl(R^{-\alpha }|f|_0+[f]_\alpha \bigr)|x-\bar x|^\alpha . \end{equation}

□
